Hardware-in-the-loop
slides.body:
- This history of HIL simulation in the automotive industry has its roots in the 1980s with the advent of
microprocessor-based ECUs for engine controls.
- Over time HIL simulation branched out into other areas such as aerospace, military, naval, and
robotics, and especially automotive industries.
- HIL simulation allows to keep the features of both computer simulation and vehicle testing by
having the real controller present, while simultaneously allowing for test scenarios to be adjusted
easily. In other words, HIL simulation provides a test platform in which the system or process under
test consists of actual hardware components while the remainder of the system or process is
simulated using physics-based or mathematical models.

slides.title: V-Cycle
slides.body:
- Shorten the time to market and reduce costs of
testing
- Reproducibility
- On-vehicle tests dangerous and not always in the
same conditions
- Scalable system
- Critical: develop an accurate model of the real
plant

slides.title: SCALEXIO
slides.body:
Features:
- Run the real-time application
- Generate sensor signals to the
ECU
- Measure command signals for
actuators
- Provide battery voltage to the ECU
- Simulate faults (FIU)

slides.title: ControlDesk
slides.body:
- Experimenting software for online testing
- Access to the calibration, measuring and
diagnostics of the ECU
- Data acquisition synchronized on ECUs, RCP
and HIL platforms and bus systems
- Enhanced layout, instrumentation, measuring
and post-processing
- Support for all the dSPACE hardware and
virtual validation platforms

slides.title: ControlDesk – Bus Navigator
slides.body:
The Bus Navigator displays bus configurations.
A bus configuration is the configuration of all the controllers,
communication matrices, and messages/frames/PDUs of a
specific communication bus such as CAN.
Simulation applications built with one of the following contain a
bus configuration:
- RTI CAN MultiMessage Blockset
- RTI LIN MultiMessage Blockset
Through the Bus Navigator communication controllers,
networks, nodes, messages and signals can be managed.
